units.title: Observability
units.rationale: Durable claims: you will not be attached to the failing process; a debugger is usually unavailable; the only practical evidence is automatically collected telemetry that can answer questions you did not know to ask. Caveat preserved: literal 'arbitrary questions' is an unbounded investment; 'sufficiently observable' to keep the promised service level is the real bar. rust-skills teaches emission, fields, and stable event names so later questions are queryable, but it never defines that product bar or separates instrumentation from the out-of-scope backend/query-tool half.

units.title: Logging
units.rationale: Durable claim: logs are the default telemetry operators reach for when something fails. The unit then describes a log record as a line of free text. rust-skills accepts logs as a telemetry kind but treats unstructured line text as the anti-pattern: events need levels, structure, and (via later units) spans. units.title: The Facade Pattern

That is exactly obs-library-facade. Filter via an environment variable with an info fallback is obs-levels-filter (prefer try_from_default_env plus a default directive). units.title: Interactions With External Systems

Missing is the support-triage framing: pick a searchable non-PII key operators can use from a user report.

units.title: Logs Must Be Easy To Correlate

Caveat preserved: noisy dependency info (sqlx at INFO) should be filtered, not deleted from the extract. obs-instrument-spans exists specifically so concurrent async work does not mix context; request.id-style fields are the structured form. Stamping a UUID into interpolated message strings is the pre-span technique the later units and rust-skills replace. HTTP-edge minting vs handler minting is refined in 4.5.14.

units.title: Structured Logging

units.title: tracing’s Span

TRACE-level enter/exit noise revealing poll count is a debugging illustration, not a separate rule. The unit's leftover error event sitting outside the query span is an acknowledged gap later fixed.

units.title: Internal Errors
units.rationale: Independent claim: failures between in-process callers are a distinct location from the external edge. rust-skills talks about Result, domain types, and operator logs, but it does not name an internal-versus-edge location axis or say that the same failure has different duties at each place. Caller-reaction and operator-report mechanics live in the child units.

units.title: Enable The Caller To React
units.rationale: Durable clauses: a payload-less failure signal is enough only when there is a single mode; callers must be forced to acknowledge success and failure; distinct modes exist so the caller can retry one class and abandon another. Result, typed enums, exhaustive match, and ? cover the mechanism. Two caveats are not skill contracts: (1) a unit error type is explicitly insufficient once reactions diverge; (2) holding up a large public infrastructure enum as the reaction surface conflicts with err-canonical-struct, which wants opaque structs and is_* helpers on evolving library APIs.

units.title: Help An Operator To Troubleshoot
units.rationale: Even a single failure mode still needs a human-readable report. In a service that report is usually a log or trace; in a CLI it is a terminal line gated by verbosity. rust-skills covers attaching context, preserving source, and emitting a full chain, plus filter directives. It does not state operator-report as a first-class purpose of the error value itself, nor that API logs and CLI verbose output are two renderings of the same duty. The unit's log-then-return illustration is later rejected by the log-once rule.

units.title: Errors At The Edge
units.rationale: Independent claim: the external caller is a different audience from an in-process function. Adjacent rules forbid leaking secrets and require Result for recoverable failure. No current rule names the edge as its own error location or assigns machine tokens versus human body text to that location. User-visible content is judged in the child unit.

units.title: Help A User To Troubleshoot
units.rationale: Three durable clauses: an unexpected internal failure should signal a generic machine status and hide internals; a caller-fixable input failure must tell the human what to change; a validation type that carries an explanation is wasted if the edge drops it. Parse-don't-validate and newtypes cover constructing the validated value. Nothing states the information budget (empty unexpected response is acceptable; empty reject-the-input response is a defect). Returning a bare String as the parse error is a skill anti-pattern, not a target.

units.title: Summary
units.rationale: Load-bearing recap: purpose is control flow or reporting; location is internal or edge; control flow must be machine-scriptable (internal types/methods/fields, edge status codes); reports are human and audience-tuned (internal logs/traces with maximal operator context, edge body with only what the user can change). Caveat: user and operator roles blur when the human has source or runs the binary; a verbosity or env knob must declare which audience to serve. rust-skills has the cells' mechanisms but not the matrix, the information-budget rule, or the blur-plus-knob caveat.

units.title: Error Reporting For Operators
units.rationale: Independent parent: operator reporting is judged from the outcome record of the failed request, not from a scavenger hunt through inner events. A suite that only asserts the status code can still ship empty exception fields. obs-error-chain and observable-coverage tests are adjacent; neither requires the handling-edge record to carry brief and chain-complete cause text, nor treats inability to explain a 5xx from that record as a defect. Book-era subscriber and formatter pins are obsolete tool versions, not the claim.

units.title: Keeping Track Of The Error Root Cause
units.rationale: Durable clauses: dropping the error value when synthesizing an edge success-typed failure response starves later reporters; a foreign response trait cannot be implemented on a foreign infrastructure error (orphan rule) and should not be, because the same cause can deserve different edge outcomes; wrap in a local type; Debug is the faithful programmer dump, Display is the brief description, and Display is not derived. Newtype coherence, common traits, and the Display/Debug split are covered. Framework-specific response traits are project-local. Missing: a rule that the error value must reach the handling edge, and that HTTP mapping must not be attached to the storage error.

units.title: The Error Trait
units.rationale: A good error is marked with std::error::Error, offers Debug and Display for different audiences, and can expose a cause through source. Result itself accepts any E; the trait is a semantic and ecosystem contract, not a language requirement. rust-skills' custom-type, source-chain, Display/Debug, and thiserror rules are that triad. Obsolete residue: treating backtrace as an unstable Error method; current skill guidance captures Backtrace in the constructor under environment policy. Error-handling WG process notes are not a coding contract.

units.title: Trait Objects

The error-API rationale—keep the cause type hidden at the Error surface—and the caveat that frequent downcast is a design smell are not written down. Convention conflict, not absence: the unit hand-writes Debug as a 'Caused by' walk and keeps Display brief, while type-display-vs-debug prefers derived Debug and err-canonical-struct may fold cause into Display and leave source empty to avoid double printing. units.title: Errors For Control Flow

units.title: Layering
units.rationale: A storage or domain failure must stay usable from a CLI or from another HTTP route that wants a different status. Choosing the edge status is the entrypoint's concern; implementing a web response trait on the inner error leaks protocol into a protocol-unaware layer. Adjacent rules stop third-party types from becoming public currency and encourage situation-specific error types. None forbids attaching transport mapping to the inner error or requires a distinct handler-layer type that owns status and body.
units.resolution: The audit gap is resolved by the mapped rule set in this change; the rationale records the pre-synthesis finding.

units.title: Modelling Errors as Enums
units.rationale: A closed set of matchable variants, From impls so ? converts, and exhaustive match to pick different edge outcomes is exactly the typed-error cluster. Later units retract per-call variants as a ball of mud; that retraction is not this unit's claim. Defaulting every variant to an unexpected status is a local framework default, not a missing skill rule.
units.resolution: The mapped pre-existing rule set already covers the durable contract and its caveats.

units.title: The Error Type Is Not Enough
units.rationale: The same source type can arise from different caller intentions (pool checkout versus insert versus commit). Situation text cannot be recovered from the type alone, so either split the situation or attach context at the call site; a single From<Source> is illegal when several variants share that source, and map_err is the correct boundary. err-from-impl already requires map_err when conversion needs call-site context; err-context-chain is the situation-text rule. Splitting one enum into more variants is a stepping stone the next section replaces with opaque-plus-context.
units.resolution: The mapped pre-existing rule set already covers the durable contract and its caveats.

units.title: Removing The Boilerplate With thiserror
units.rationale: Derive Display, source, and From instead of hand-writing them. #[error] owns Display (with field interpolation); #[source] owns the cause; #[from] is From plus source. A String field cannot be a source because it is not an Error. That is the thiserror rule. Style conflict: current lowercase-no-trailing-punctuation guidance rejects the unit's sentence-case messages. Crate major pin in the extract is a snapshot, not the contract.
units.resolution: The mapped pre-existing rule set already covers the durable contract and its caveats.

units.title: Avoid “Ball Of Mud” Error Enums
units.rationale: Variants that simultaneously encode every internal call and the edge response freeze implementation details and do not scale. A caller of the handler layer can act only on distinctions at that layer (here: fixable input versus unexpected). Unexpected must stay opaque; forwarding a raw cause through transparent Display without new situation text drops the operator sentence. err-canonical-struct already rejects crate-wide catch-all enums. Missing: the layering rule that a type exposes only distinctions its caller can act on, and that diagnostic richness belongs in the source chain rather than in extra public variants. Boxing dyn Error because it is unsized is language mechanics already implied by trait-dyn-vs-generic.
units.resolution: The audit gap is resolved by the mapped rule set in this change; the rationale records the pre-synthesis finding.

units.title: Using anyhow As Opaque Error Type
units.rationale: Prefer a Send + Sync + 'static opaque wrapper that can capture a backtrace and accept context, instead of a hand-rolled box-plus-string pair. context both converts and records caller intent so ? stays clean. That is err-anyhow-app plus err-context-chain. The Context-on-Result delivery is an extension trait, already described. eyre-class alternatives are acknowledged in the same skill rule as equivalent facades, provided the application picks one.
units.resolution: The mapped pre-existing rule set already covers the durable contract and its caveats.

units.title: anyhow Or thiserror?
units.rationale: The durable criterion is caller intent: if this caller must branch, publish a matchable type (thiserror helps); if this caller should only report and stop, publish an opaque error (anyhow, eyre, or a boxed Error). Crate role is a heuristic, not the rule—libraries often ship enums because they refuse to assume intent, at the cost of a large match surface, and an opaque library error is sometimes correct. rust-skills still titles the split as library-versus-application even though later rows and err-canonical-struct already describe match-versus-report and opaque library structs. The myth the unit rejects remains the skill's headline framing.
units.resolution: The audit gap is resolved by the mapped rule set in this change; the rationale records the pre-synthesis finding.

units.title: Who Should Log Errors?
units.rationale: Log an error when it is handled. A function that propagates with ? must not also emit an error-level record; it may attach context. If the failure reaches the process edge, a single dedicated reporter owns the record. Duplicate error-level lines make operators unsure whether they are seeing one failure or several. That is obs-error-chain (log-once, full chain, warn only if absorbed). Which HTTP middleware emits the edge record is project-local; a promised framework-log removal is a snapshot.
